user_input: My refund was approved 15 days ago, but I still haven't received the money.
expected: Identify gateway delay; cite E-commerce Rules 2020; suggest bank statement verification and escalation.
actual_response:
[LawPilot AI — Grounded Demo Mode]

### 🛒 Consumer Rights Analysis: Defective Product & Refund Refusal

**1. Legal Assessment of Your Situation:**
You purchased a product that turned out defective, and the seller/platform is unlawfully refusing a refund or replacement.

**2. Applicable Indian Consumer Laws:**
- **[The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — Section 2(47)](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/15256)**: Unfair Trade Practice and Refusal to Take Back Defective Goods or Refund
- **[Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 — Rule 4 & Rule 6](https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/sites/default/files/E-commerce%20Rules.pdf)**: Duties of E-Commerce Entities & Grievance Redressal Mechanism
- **[The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — Section 2(7)](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/15256)**: Definition of Consumer (Including E-commerce and Offline Purchases)
- **[The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — Section 35 & Section 38](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/15256)**: Manner in which complaint shall be made and Procedure before District Commission
- **Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 2(47)):** Refusing to withdraw defective goods or refund consideration within the agreed period (or within 30 days) constitutes an explicit **Unfair Trade Practice**.
- **Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 35 & 84):** Gives consumers the right to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission and claim product liability damages.
- **Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020:** Mandates platforms to accept returns and resolve consumer complaints within 30 days.

**3. Essential Evidence to Preserve:**
- Purchase tax invoice / order receipt.
- Photos or unboxing video demonstrating the defect.
- Customer support communication and rejection emails.

**4. Practical Next Steps:**
1. **National Consumer Helpline (NCH):** Register a complaint immediately via **1915** or online at https://consumerhelpline.gov.in/.
2. **Issue a Formal Refund Notice:** Send a registered 15-day demand notice.
3. **File via e-Daakhil:** Submit an e-complaint before the District Consumer Commission without requiring a lawyer.

👉 **Next Question for You:** What was the total purchase price paid for the defective product?

citations.title: Unfair Trade Practice and Refusal to Take Back Defective Goods or Refund
citations.description: Refusing to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration contemplated within the period stipulated, or within 30 days if no period is stipulated, constitutes an unfair trade practice.

citations.title: Duties of E-Commerce Entities & Grievance Redressal Mechanism
citations.description: Every e-commerce entity shall establish an adequate grievance redressal mechanism and appoint a Grievance Officer whose details are displayed on its platform. The officer must acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and redress the complaint within one month.

citations.title: Definition of Consumer (Including E-commerce and Offline Purchases)
citations.description: Defines a consumer as any person who buys goods or hires/avails any services for a consideration paid or promised, including offline or online transactions through electronic means or by teleshopping or direct selling.

citations.title: Manner in which complaint shall be made and Procedure before District Commission
citations.description: A complaint in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer, including online through the e-Daakhil portal.
